title: Diffusion-like overpotentials from non-diffusion mechanisms in battery particles - Nature Energy
gist: A Stanford/MIT/Seoul National University team shows that the square-root-of-time overpotentials universally read as solid-state lithium diffusion in NMC cathode particles can instead arise from electrolyte-penetrated pores inside agglomerates, which form a transmission-line chemical capacitance that mimics diffusion. Changing only the liquid electrolyte shifts the apparent diffusion overpotential of LixNi1/3Mn1/3Co1/3O2 even in thin electrodes, implying that published Li chemical diffusion coefficients and charge-transfer resistances are systematically misassigned.

insights.claim: Battery diffusivities extracted from square-root-of-time overpotential behaviour span four orders of magnitude across the literature, a spread large enough to indicate the measurement interpretation itself is wrong rather than material variation.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Any battery materials thesis or diligence model resting on published Li diffusivity values as a screening or ranking metric is built on numbers with 10,000x internal disagreement.

insights.claim: The paper argues explicitly that the Li chemical diffusion coefficients and charge-transfer resistances already reported in the literature should be revisited, not just measured more carefully going forward.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Expect a wave of re-analysis papers and possible retraction of performance claims in cathode-materials startups whose differentiation rests on measured diffusivity or charge-transfer improvements.

insights.claim: Electroanalytical practice should shift from assuming solid-state diffusion a priori to identifying the specific physical origin of an observed overpotential signature.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Battery characterization tooling and services that can discriminate mechanism (not just fit a Warburg element) gain a defensible position as this becomes the expected standard.
insights.quote: Electroanalytical methods should therefore seek to identify specific physical origins rather than assume solid-state diffusion a priori.

insights.claim: Electrolyte-penetrating pores inside agglomerate cathode particles can generate diffusion-like kinetics even when no diffusion process is occurring at all.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: The single largest structural variable in cathode performance measurement may be particle porosity, which is a manufacturing/processing parameter rather than an intrinsic material property.
insights.quote: electrolyte-penetrating pores in agglomerate particles can generate diffusion-like kinetics even without any diffusion processes

insights.claim: The mechanism is that electrolyte-penetrated pores produce a transmission-line configuration in chemical capacitance, and it is that circuit topology, not mass transport, that yields the square-root-of-time signature.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Provides a concrete, testable discriminator: geometry-driven transmission-line behaviour should scale with porosity and electrolyte properties, while true solid diffusion should not.
insights.quote: Electrolyte-penetrated pores produce a transmission-line configuration in chemical capacitance, leading to diffusion-like electrochemical behaviour.

insights.claim: Square-root-of-time overpotential behaviour is not exclusive to diffusion, so the observation cannot by itself identify a transport mechanism.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Undermines the decades-old default inference used across academic and industrial battery labs; anyone whose QC pipeline hard-codes this assumption is producing misleading numbers.
insights.quote: This demonstration highlights that square-root-of-time overpotentials are not exclusive to diffusion.

insights.claim: A rate distribution analysis is used to contrast diffusion-like impedance in a porous particle against genuine solid-state chemical diffusion in a dense particle, positioning porosity versus density as the key experimental contrast.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Suggests dense single-crystal cathodes and porous polycrystalline agglomerates are not comparable on the same electroanalytical metrics, complicating cross-supplier benchmarking.

insights.claim: Modifying only the liquid electrolyte increases the apparent diffusion overpotential of LixNi1/3Mn1/3Co1/3O2 particles, even in thin electrodes where bulk electrolyte transport limitations should be negligible.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: A property assumed to be intrinsic to the solid cathode turns out to be tunable by the electrolyte formulation, so electrolyte suppliers may hold more of the performance lever than cathode makers.

insights.claim: The thin-electrode control is the decisive element of the argument, because thin electrodes are the standard configuration used precisely to eliminate electrolyte transport as an explanation.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Removes the easiest rebuttal, which makes the finding much harder for incumbent methodology defenders to dismiss and raises the odds it propagates quickly.

insights.claim: Apparent Warburg coefficients were measured as a function of salt concentration for two chemically distinct salts, LiPF6 and LiClO4, showing the effect is a general electrolyte-concentration phenomenon rather than a quirk of one salt chemistry.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Two-salt replication makes the result robust; treat it as likely to survive peer scrutiny rather than as a single-system artefact.

insights.claim: The effect appears even in single-crystalline LixNi0.83Mn0.05Co0.12O2 particles with a non-porous morphology, and the apparent Warburg coefficients show a lack of correlation with charge-transfer resistance.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Single-crystal high-nickel cathodes, the industry's favoured next-generation format, are not immune, so the measurement problem extends to the materials being commercialized right now.

insights.so_what: Commercial-grade material means cell makers using merchant cathode powders face the same misattribution in their own internal characterization.

themes.theme: Who is behind the result and why it matters commercially

insights.claim: The work was funded by the Toyota Research Institute through its Accelerated Materials Design and Discovery programme, meaning a major automaker's research arm is bankrolling a result that invalidates standard battery characterization practice.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: OEM-funded methodology critiques usually precede internal spec changes; watch whether Toyota's cell qualification criteria shift away from diffusivity-based screening.
insights.quote: This work was supported by the Toyota Research Institute through the Accelerated Materials Design and Discovery programme.

insights.claim: The author list concentrates unusual authority, combining Stanford and the SLAC-Stanford Battery Center under William C. Chueh with MIT's Martin Z. Bazant, the field's leading electrochemical modelling theorist.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Credibility of the messengers raises the probability that this reframing becomes consensus quickly rather than being contested for a decade.

insights.claim: Additional funding came from the National Research Foundation of Korea via the Institute for Battery Research Innovation, with Seoul National University co-authors, indicating parallel Korean institutional investment in re-examining battery metrology.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Korea's battery ecosystem is funding the same metrology rethink, a signal that cell makers there may already be discounting literature diffusivity values.

insights.claim: The team built a dedicated three-electrode coin cell platform to run the measurements, implying the standard two-electrode coin cell used across the industry cannot cleanly separate these effects.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Creates demand for three-electrode test hardware and for reference-electrode-capable cell formats in battery R&D labs.

insights.claim: Establishing the porosity story required a stack of physical characterization methods including mercury porosimetry, particle size analysis, pycnometry and nano-computed tomography, none of which are routine in electrochemical papers.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Correctly interpreting cathode kinetics now demands multi-modal structural metrology, raising the cost and the equipment barrier for credible battery materials claims.

insights.claim: The paper was received on 25 October 2025 and accepted 7 July 2026, an unusually long roughly eight-and-a-half-month review for a result that overturns standard practice.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Long contested review plus named reviewers signals the claim was fought over, so anticipate published rebuttals and treat immediate consensus as unlikely.

insights.claim: Both the experimental data behind the electrolyte-concentration results and the code reproducing the agglomerate model are publicly deposited, lowering the barrier for third parties to replicate or refute the claim.
insights.speaker: Nature Energy
insights.so_what: Open data plus open model means verification will be fast, so the thesis will be confirmed or broken within months, not years.
